subject: Forensic access obligations, evidence handback & transfer mapping
messages:
From: Security Team <security@medmatch.health>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.example>
Cc: Legal - MedMatch <legal@medmatch.health>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible customer data exposure — initial request for evidence and timeline

Hi Sean,

We're investigating an event that may involve user metadata processed via Redwood's API for our integration. At this stage we believe a subset of user IDs (approximately ~1,800 records) may have been temporarily exposed through a misconfigured S3 link on our side, but we'd like to confirm if any Redwood logs or cached payloads include customer-identifying attributes.

Can Redwood provide: 1) a short-form initial notification stating whether customer plaintext was present in logs/kv cache, 2) a copy of any request/response logs for the impacted integration (timespan: 2027-06-28 00:00 UTC to 2027-06-29 23:59 UTC), and 3) a statement of the retention and chain-of-custody you will apply to any evidence you hand back?

Timing is sensitive — our counsel has asked for an initial status within 48 hours and a fuller evidence packet within 7 business days. Please also confirm whether Redwood requires an NDA/DSA or a DocuSign addendum tied to cross-border transfer before we exchange hashed identifiers.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Security Ops 
MedMatch Health
[attachment: incident_summary.txt (txt)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.example>
To: Elena Morales <security@medmatch.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible customer data exposure — initial request for evidence and timeline

Elena — thanks for flagging and for the detail. We can support the requests but want to align on the contractual obligations and scope so we don't inadvertently over-share. Summary of our proposed approach:

- Initial acknowledgement: we will provide an initial status email within 48 hours confirming whether Redwood observed any plaintext PII in production request logs or in serving KV caches for the timeframe you listed.

- Evidence window & preservation: Redwood will preserve relevant logs and KV cache dumps for 21 days from initial notice to allow for joint forensics, with a manifest and cryptographic hashes produced for chain-of-custody. We can provide the manifest as a CSV and hash values.

- Forensic access & handback: we can provide an encrypted evidence bundle (S3 link + manifest) under a scoped access agreement. If MedMatch requires raw request payloads that include customer identifiers, we typically require either a mutual NDA or an executed DSA addendum that permits cross-border transfer where applicable. Alternatively, we can provide redacted payloads plus per-record hashes to enable matching.

- Subprocessor coordination: if the data touched any third-party subprocessors (e.g., managed logging providers), we'll coordinate with them but ask for a joint request so we can track permissions and SLAs.

Action items:
1) Marissa: please confirm exact log buckets and the retention snapshot we can lock.
2) Ben: prepare the forensic-request-template.docx and evidence_manifest.csv with the hashing schema (SHA256).
3) Neha/legal: advise on whether a limited DSA addendum or DocuSign flow is required for the temporary transfer of hashed vs raw payloads.

I'll follow up with the initial status note by 10:00 AM PT tomorrow.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Security Liaison
Redwood Inference
[attachment: forensic-request-template.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible customer data exposure — initial request for evidence and timeline

Adding a couple operational clarifications from infra/ops:

- Hashing & match approach: we'll compute SHA256 for request payloads and include a salted hash for PII fields to avoid returning raw identifiers. If MedMatch confirms they need the raw values, we should insist on an executed data transfer addendum (DTA) or the signed DocuSign link.

- Forensic scope / storage: the preserved snapshot will be stored in a segregated S3 bucket with object-level encryption. Access will be via pre-signed URL and ephemeral keys; we'll rotate keys after download. Retention: we lock snapshots for 21 days but can extend by request for an additional 30 days for active investigations.

- Subprocessor mapping: if logs were forwarded to our logging partner (LogStream Inc.), we'll need a written consent or joint-authorized request to pull those logs because they are covered under our subprocessor terms in the DPA. We'll ask MedMatch to provide an authorized contact and scope (log indices/time ranges).

I've uploaded a draft evidence_manifest.csv to our shared drive and seeded it with the hash schema. Link: https://drive.redwood.company/shared/MedMatch-Forensics-2027

Ben
Senior Platform Ops
Redwood Inference
[attachment: evidence_manifest.csv (csv)]

From: Legal - MedMatch <legal@medmatch.health>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.example>
Cc: Elena Morales <security@medmatch.health>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible customer data exposure — initial request for evidence and timeline

Sean, Ben — thanks. We're comfortable with the 48-hour initial status and the 21-day preservation window you propose, provided we receive the manifest and hashes within 7 business days. A few clarifications from counsel:

- DocuSign addendum: MedMatch can execute a limited DTA via DocuSign for the purposes of temporary transfer of raw payloads. Please send the prepared DTA link and a redlined scope showing exactly which fields would be transferred. If Redwood can provide hashed matches first, we prefer to avoid transferring raw PII unless absolutely necessary.

- Subprocessor consent: we will provide the authorized contact for LogStream Inc. by EOD Monday and confirm the scope (indices and time ranges). We expect Redwood to coordinate and produce any subprocessor-specific evidence within the same 21-day preservation window.

- Chain of custody: please ensure the manifest includes SHA256 hashes, timestamps (UTC), object paths, and the name of the Redwood engineer who prepared the bundle. We will countersign a limited receipt acknowledgement on delivery.

Action items we will complete:
1) Elena: prepare the authorized contact details for LogStream Inc.
2) Legal: sign the DTA once we receive the DocuSign envelope.

Appreciate the quick collaboration — please share the initial status note when available.

Regards,
Ravi Patel
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
MedMatch Health
